key_insight: Large language model–based agents (Claude Code) can autonomously perform the full experimental high energy physics analysis pipeline— from event selection through statistical inference and paper drafting—given a dataset, an execution framework, and relevant literature.
problem_solved: Reduces the expert time and manual effort required to run end-to-end experimental HEP analyses by automating routine and complex pipeline stages with minimal curated input.
method: Provide the agent with a HEP dataset, an execution environment, and a corpus of prior experimental literature.
Use the LLM to generate, run, and iteratively refine analysis code for event selection, background estimation, uncertainty quantification, and statistical inference.
Automate synthesis and composition of results into written draft text while validating outputs via experiment-style checks and uncertainty reporting.
impact: Accelerates prototyping, reproducibility, and scaling of experimental analyses and lowers the barrier for AI/ML practitioners to engage in HEP workflows—while highlighting the continuing need for expert oversight and validation.
visual_elements: Pipeline flowchart: agent-centered diagram showing inputs (data, code environment, literature) feeding automated stages (selection → background → uncertainties → inference → paper).
Before/After bar chart: comparison of expert effort/time versus agent-automated time for each pipeline stage.
Code-to-run loop: small diagram illustrating LLM code generation, execution, test, and iteration cycle.
Validation dashboard mockup: visual of uncertainty bands, background fits, and a checklist indicating human review points.
paper_title: AI Agents Can Already Autonomously Perform Experimental High Energy Physics
paper_authors: Eric A. Moreno, Samuel Bright-Thonney, Andrzej Novak, Dolores Garcia, Philip Harris
